purpose: a put_on restriction is checked on the block-target branch and on the surface branch; failure of the block branch's clearance does not refute the surface branch
text: There is a robot hand. Block a and block b are blocks. The hand holds block a. Block b is on the table. Block b is clear. Block a is not dry. The hand can put a block on something only if the block is dry.

units.text: Block a and block b are blocks.
Block b is on the table.
The hand can put a block on something only if the block is dry.

must_have.note: the hook must be required by BOTH library paths poss_put_on_block and poss_put_on_surface

must_not_have.note: no clause may conclude -poss(put_on) from -clear_top(Y) alone: the surface branch does not need clearance (A4.2)

queries.text: Can the hand put block a on block b now?

expect.evidence: S7 necessity with -dry(a) at W0; the block branch would otherwise succeed (holding, isa block b, clear_top b, differ a b)

queries.text: Can the hand put block a on the table now?

expect.evidence: the same restriction on the surface branch

variants.text: There is a robot hand. Block a and block b are blocks. The hand holds block a. Block b is on the table. Block b is clear. Block a is dry. The hand can put a block on something only if the block is dry.

expect.evidence: block branch (poss_put_on_hand_block): holding(hand,a), isa block b, clear_top(b) at W0, differ(a,b); S7 via dry(a) at W0
surface branch (poss_put_on_hand_surface): holding(hand,a) at W0, surface(table) from the library; S7 via dry(a) at W0

variants.text: There is a robot hand. Block a and block b are blocks. The hand holds block a. Block b is on the table. Block b is not clear. Block a is dry. The hand can put a block on something only if the block is dry.

expect.evidence: the block branch fails (-clear_top(b) at W0); the surface branch is not established for a block (surface(b) is not derivable) and not refuted. No clause concludes -poss(put_on) from -clear_top alone, so there is no negative proof. Missing positive proof is not negative proof (A2.3). A library law 'a block is not a surface' would exclude the surface branch but would still not supply -poss, so it would not turn this into No (REVIEW.md disposition 5); no such law is added.
surface branch with dry(a) at W0; b's clearance is irrelevant to the table

candidates.reason: replay: block branch needs clear_top(b) (false); surface branch needs surface(b) (unsupported in the finite model). Not validated. The replay's 'invalid' is a validation verdict, not a proof of impossibility.

explain: The library has two poss laws for put_on. A restriction hook added to only one of them leaves a bypass. Q1 and Q2 fail for the same reason on different branches. The dry_b_occupied variant is the A4.2 sentence about branches: Q1 is Unknown, not No, because the surface branch is neither established nor refuted for a block, and no necessity clause mentions clearance. The replay rejects the candidate as not validated (K1), which is a validation result, not an impossibility proof.
notes: Amended 2026-09-11: the first version asked whether a 'block is not a surface' law would give No; the review corrected the premise (such a law removes one positive branch and supplies no negative).
